name: Chicken Pizza
description: Homemade chicken pizza with a soft yeast crust, cooked seasoned chicken, vegetables, pizza sauce and bubbling mozzarella.
ingredients: 0.75 cup warm water, added gradually as needed
250 g boneless chicken, cooked and seasoned
Oregano, salt and cooking oil, as needed
method: Combine the flour, instant yeast, sugar and salt. Add the warm water gradually with a little oil and knead until you have a soft, smooth dough rather than a wet sticky mixture.
Cover the dough and leave it in a warm place until it has risen to nearly double its original size.
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Gently deflate the risen dough, shape or roll it to fit the pizza tray and leave a slightly thicker rim if desired.
Spread the pizza sauce over the base, leaving the edge mostly clear, then distribute the already cooked seasoned chicken, capsicum and onion evenly.
Cover with mozzarella and sprinkle with oregano. Avoid piling all wet toppings in the centre, which can make the middle slower to bake.
Bake in the fully preheated oven until the crust is cooked and golden at the edges and the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Rest for a few minutes so the cheese settles slightly, then slice and serve hot.
image_alt: Homemade chicken pizza with golden yeast crust, seasoned chicken, capsicum, onion and melted mozzarella
image_caption: Chicken pizza baked on a risen yeast crust with cooked chicken, vegetables and bubbling mozzarella.
technique: The crust needs a soft dough and a real rise before baking. Keep toppings relatively dry and the chicken already cooked so the oven can focus on setting the crust and melting cheese rather than steaming a wet centre.
doneness_cues: Dough should expand close to double before shaping.
Base should feel soft and elastic, not stiff and cracked.
Crust edges should be golden and the underside cooked through.
Cheese should be melted and bubbling without the centre remaining doughy.
mistakes: Using wet tomato or vegetable toppings that flood the centre.
Loading raw chicken onto a short-bake pizza.
Rolling dough too thin at the centre while leaving very wet toppings there.
Cutting immediately while molten cheese and steam make slices collapse.
substitutions: Use cooked tikka-style chicken for a spicier Pakistani variation.
Part whole-wheat flour can be used but may require more water and a denser crust.
Reduce cheese rather than increasing bake time if you want a lighter pizza.
reheating: Reheat in an oven, air fryer or covered pan until hot; this keeps the crust better than a long microwave cycle.
serving: Rest 3 to 5 minutes after baking, then slice and serve.
